title: Micah Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Micah chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Micah Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Micah Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:1, when do the wicked work evil?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:1 states that the wicked work evil 'when the morning is light.'

questions.question: What do the wicked covet and take by violence according to Micah 2:2?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:2 explains that the wicked covet fields and houses and take them by violence.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 2:3 says that the LORD devises good things against the family mentioned.
questions.explanation: Micah 2:3 states that the LORD devises an evil against this family, not good things.

questions.question: In Micah 2:4, what is said to be changed and removed?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:4 mentions that 'he hath changed the portion of my people' and removed it.

questions.question: What will the people have none of in the congregation of the LORD as stated in Micah 2:5?
options: None that shall cast a cord by lot
questions.correctAnswer: None that shall cast a cord by lot
questions.explanation: Micah 2:5 says, 'thou shalt have none that shall cast a cord by lot in the congregation of the LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: In Micah 2:6, people tell the prophets not to prophesy to avoid shame.
questions.explanation: Micah 2:6 records people saying to the prophets, 'Prophesy ye not... they shall not take shame.'

questions.question: According to Micah 2:7, what is questioned about the house of Jacob?
options: Is the spirit of the LORD straitened?
Do they follow the law faithfully?
questions.correctAnswer: Is the spirit of the LORD straitened?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:7 asks, 'O thou that art named the house of Jacob, is the spirit of the LORD straitened?'

questions.question: Who are described as pulling off the robe with the garment from those passing securely in Micah 2:8?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:8 says, 'Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off the robe with the garment...'

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 2:9, the women of the people have been welcomed into pleasant houses.
questions.explanation: Micah 2:9 states the women have been cast out from their pleasant houses, not welcomed.

questions.question: What command is given in Micah 2:10?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:10 commands, 'Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest.'

questions.question: According to Micah 2:11, what will a man lying and prophesying about wine and strong drink become?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:11 says such a man 'shall even be the prophet of this people.'

questions.question: Who does the LORD say He will gather like sheep in Micah 2:12?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:12 states the LORD will gather 'the remnant of Israel' as sheep.

questions.question: What does the breaker do before the people in Micah 2:13?
options: Breaks up and passes through the gate
Builds a wall around the city
Leads a procession to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Breaks up and passes through the gate
questions.explanation: Micah 2:13 describes the breaker as coming up before them, breaking up, and passing through the gate.

questions.question: In Micah 2, which event comes first?
options: The LORD devises an evil against the family
People covet and take fields by violence
The breaker passes through the gate
The remnant of Israel is gathered
questions.correctAnswer: People covet and take fields by violence
questions.explanation: Micah 2:2 describes people coveting and taking fields by violence before the LORD's devising evil in 2:3, the gathering in 2:12, and the breaker passing in 2:13.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 2:1 describes the wicked as devising iniquity and working evil on their beds.
questions.explanation: Micah 2:1 clearly states, 'Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds!'

medium.title: Micah Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Micah Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:6, what do the people say to those who prophesy?
options: Prophesy not, lest you take shame
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesy not, lest you take shame
questions.explanation: Micah 2:6 states that they say to the prophets, 'Prophesy ye not,' so that they shall not take shame. This reflects the rejection of true prophecy by the people, as also seen in Micah 2:7 where God questions if His spirit is straitened by their rejection.

questions.question: How does Micah 2:7 describe the effect of God's words on those who walk uprightly?
options: They do good to those who walk uprightly
questions.correctAnswer: They do good to those who walk uprightly
questions.explanation: Micah 2:7 explains that God's words do good to the one who walks uprightly, contrasting with the rejection of prophecy in the same verse. This shows the blessing and benefit of obedience.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:8 accuse the people of doing to others who pass by securely?
options: Pulling off the robe with the garment
questions.correctAnswer: Pulling off the robe with the garment
questions.explanation: Micah 2:8 describes how the people have risen as enemies, pulling off the robe along with the garment from those who pass by securely. This depicts exploitative behavior and injustice.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:9, what have the people done to the women of God's people?
options: Cast them out from their pleasant houses
questions.correctAnswer: Cast them out from their pleasant houses
questions.explanation: Micah 2:9 states that the women of God's people have been cast out from their pleasant houses, and their children taken away, indicating severe oppression and loss.

questions.question: What warning does Micah 2:10 give to the people about their current place of rest?
options: It is a place of peace and safety
It is not their rest and is polluted
It will become a place of prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: It is not their rest and is polluted
questions.explanation: Micah 2:10 commands the people to arise and depart because 'this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction,' warning of impending judgment.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:11 say about a man who lies and claims to prophesy about wine and strong drink?
options: He shall be the prophet of the people
He shall be condemned and punished
He shall be ignored by the people
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be the prophet of the people
questions.explanation: Micah 2:11 states that if a man walking in falsehood lies saying he will prophesy of wine and strong drink, he will indeed be considered the prophet of the people, highlighting the corruption of false prophecy.

questions.question: How does Micah 2:12 describe the gathering of Israel?
options: As scattered birds in the wilderness
As the sheep of Bozrah in the midst of their fold
questions.correctAnswer: As the sheep of Bozrah in the midst of their fold
questions.explanation: Micah 2:12 promises that God will assemble the remnant of Israel together as sheep in their fold, emphasizing restoration and unity under God's care.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:13, who goes before the people when they pass through the gate?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:13 states that their king passes before them, and the LORD is on the head of them, symbolizing divine leadership and protection during their deliverance.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:7 teach about the relationship between God's spirit and the actions of the house of Jacob?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:7 questions if the spirit of the LORD is straitened and if the injustices are His doings, concluding that God's words are good to the upright. This affirms God's spirit is not limited by their wrongdoing.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 2:6 indicates that the people encourage prophets to speak boldly without fear of shame.
questions.explanation: Micah 2:6 shows the opposite: the people say to the prophets, 'Prophesy ye not,' to avoid taking shame, indicating rejection rather than encouragement.

questions.question: Does Micah 2:10 suggest that staying in the polluted place will bring destruction?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:10 warns the people to arise and depart because the polluted place will destroy them with a sore destruction, indicating the danger of remaining there.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity can be drawn from the behavior described in Micah 2:8 and 2:9?
options: Integrity involves exploiting others for gain
Integrity requires protecting the vulnerable and respecting others
Integrity means ignoring the needs of others
Integrity is unrelated to how we treat others' property
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity requires protecting the vulnerable and respecting others
questions.explanation: Micah 2:8-9 condemn rising as enemies and pulling off garments, casting out women, and taking away glory from children, illustrating lack of integrity. True integrity contrasts such injustice by protecting and respecting others.

questions.question: Based on Micah 2:6-7, how should a believer respond to discouragement when others reject God's word?
options: Stop sharing God’s word to avoid shame
Understand that God's spirit is not limited and His words benefit the upright
Change the message to please people
Ignore God's word and follow popular opinion
questions.correctAnswer: Understand that God's spirit is not limited and His words benefit the upright
questions.explanation: Micah 2:6-7 shows that even when people reject prophecy, God's spirit is not straitened and His words do good to the upright, encouraging believers to remain faithful despite rejection.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:12 promise will happen if the people gather as instructed in Micah 2:11?
options: They will be scattered and lost
They will be assembled as sheep in their fold, making great noise
They will be defeated by enemies
They will become silent and fearful
questions.correctAnswer: They will be assembled as sheep in their fold, making great noise
questions.explanation: Micah 2:11-12 together imply that though false prophets arise, God will gather His people as sheep in their fold, causing a great noise of multitude, symbolizing restoration and strength.

questions.question: How does Micah 2:10 relate to the warning in Micah 2:9 about casting out the women and children?
options: Micah 2:10 encourages staying because the place is safe
Micah 2:10 warns to leave because the polluted place will destroy, connecting to the injustice described in 2:9
questions.correctAnswer: Micah 2:10 warns to leave because the polluted place will destroy, connecting to the injustice described in 2:9
questions.explanation: Micah 2:9 describes injustice, and 2:10 follows by commanding departure because the polluted place (caused by such injustice) will bring destruction, linking moral failure to consequences.

hard.title: Micah Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Micah Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:11, what does the man walking in the spirit and falsehood claim he will prophesy about?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:11 states that the false prophet claims, 'I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink.'

questions.question: In Micah 2:12, the remnant of Israel is gathered together like what?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:12 compares the gathering of Israel to sheep of Bozrah being assembled as a flock in their fold.

questions.question: What title is given to the one who leads the people through the gate in Micah 2:13?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:13 identifies the leader as 'The breaker' who has broken through the gate and leads the people.

questions.question: The phrase 'the breaker' in Micah 2:13 can be seen as a typology referring to what New Testament figure?
questions.explanation: The breaker who leads the people is typologically understood as Jesus Christ who breaks the way for salvation, fulfilling the Old Testament imagery (Micah 2:13; John 10:9).

questions.question: What Hebrew term used in Micah 2:12 for 'assemble' implies a careful, purposeful gathering?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word קָבַץ (qāḇaṣ) used in Micah 2:12 means to gather or assemble carefully, indicating God's purposeful regathering of Israel.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Micah 2:4 to express the lamentation over the loss of fields?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:4 uses lamentation parallelism, repeating and amplifying the grief over the people’s land being taken and divided.

questions.question: In Micah 2:10, what reason is given for the people to 'Arise ye, and depart'?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:10 commands departure because the land is polluted and will bring destruction.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'Bozrah' in Micah 2:12, and why is it significant?
options: A sheepfold or enclosure; signifies protection
A city of refuge; signifies safety
questions.correctAnswer: A sheepfold or enclosure; signifies protection
questions.explanation: Bozrah means a sheepfold or enclosure, symbolizing the protective gathering of Israel by God (Micah 2:12).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of regathering Israel as sheep in Micah 2:12?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:12 speaks of God seeking out His sheep and gathering them, closely paralleling Micah 2:12's theme of regathering Israel.

questions.question: The phrase 'The breaker is come up before them' in Micah 2:13 is a prophetic image foreshadowing what event in Israel’s history?
questions.explanation: The breaker leading the people through gates symbolizes the messianic leader facilitating Israel’s return from exile (Micah 2:13; Isaiah 62:10).

questions.question: In Micah 2:7, the prophet questions if the spirit of the LORD is 'straitened.' What does this imply about the people's perception of God’s justice?
options: They think God is limited in power
They feel God is far away
questions.correctAnswer: They think God is limited in power
questions.explanation: Micah 2:7 challenges the idea that God's spirit is 'straitened' or limited, confronting the people's misunderstanding of God's justice and power.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:6, what do people say to the prophets to silence them?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:6 reveals that people tell prophets 'Prophesy ye not' to prevent them from speaking truth and bringing shame upon them.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 2:9 describes how women and children of God's people are cast out from their homes and glory.
questions.explanation: Micah 2:9 explicitly states that the women are cast out from their pleasant houses and children taken away God's glory.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 2:5 indicates that the people will still have lots cast by lot in the congregation of the LORD.
questions.explanation: Micah 2:5 declares there shall be none that cast a cord by lot in the congregation of the LORD, indicating loss of inheritance and land.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage can be connected to the theme of false prophecy about wine and strong drink in Micah 2:11?
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:15 warns against false prophets, connecting with Micah 2:11's condemnation of those who prophesy lies about wine and strong drink.

theological.title: Micah Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Micah Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:1 warn against those who devise iniquity?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:1 states, 'Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds!' indicating that those who plan evil face divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:3, what does the LORD devise against the family of those who oppress others?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:3 says, 'Behold, against this family do I devise an evil,' highlighting God's response to injustice.

questions.question: What is the fate of those who oppress others according to Micah 2:5?
options: None shall cast a cord by lot
questions.correctAnswer: None shall cast a cord by lot
questions.explanation: Micah 2:5 indicates that those who oppress will not have a place in the congregation of the LORD.

questions.question: What lamentation is mentioned in Micah 2:4?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:4 speaks of a 'doleful lamentation' due to the spoiling of the people, signifying deep sorrow for their plight.

questions.question: According to Micah 2:8, how have the people of Israel behaved towards others?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:8 states, 'Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy,' indicating a betrayal of trust among the people.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:11 say a false prophet would prophesy about?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:11 highlights that a man walking in falsehood would prophesy about 'wine and strong drink,' misleading the people.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:10 say about the land of Israel?
options: It is a land of rest
questions.explanation: Micah 2:10 states, 'this is not your rest: because it is polluted,' indicating the need for departure from sin.

questions.question: How does Micah 2:12 describe the gathering of Israel?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:12 describes the gathering of Israel as 'the sheep of Bozrah,' emphasizing unity and care in God's restoration.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:13 refer to as 'the breaker'?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:13 states that 'the breaker is come up before them,' referring to the LORD leading His people out of bondage.

questions.question: What warning does Micah 2:9 give about the treatment of women?
options: They have been cast out from pleasant houses
questions.correctAnswer: They have been cast out from pleasant houses
questions.explanation: Micah 2:9 indicates that the women of Israel have been unjustly cast out, showing the severity of oppression.

questions.question: What is suggested about the spirit of the LORD in Micah 2:7?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:7 questions, 'is the spirit of the LORD straitened?' indicating a limitation due to the people's actions.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:6 reveal about the people's attitude towards prophecy?
questions.explanation: Micah 2:6 states, 'Prophesy ye not, say they to them that prophesy,' showing their disdain for true prophecy.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Micah 2:2 and 2:3 convey about oppression?
options: It is a sign of strength
questions.explanation: Micah 2:2 discusses the violence used to seize property, while 2:3 warns of impending judgment for such oppression.

questions.question: What combined message do Micah 2:10 and 2:11 convey about false security?
options: It is a sign of faith
questions.explanation: Micah 2:10 warns of polluted rest, while 2:11 highlights false prophets promising comfort, both leading to destruction.

questions.question: What does Micah 2:12 and 2:13 illustrate about God's plan for Israel?
options: It is to restore and lead them
questions.correctAnswer: It is to restore and lead them
questions.explanation: Micah 2:12 speaks of gathering Israel, and 2:13 shows the LORD leading them, illustrating God's redemptive plan.
